neighbours.label: the quantifier in the idioms 'by no means' / 'by any means' (and French 'par ailleurs')
fire: The result was by no means certain when the votes were first counted.
She is not, by any means, the only scientist to question the data.
His first novel was by no means a failure, though it sold slowly.
We need to finish the bridge by any means available before winter.
The problem is by no means new; farmers have faced it for centuries.
Par ailleurs, le gouvernement a annoncé une nouvelle réforme fiscale.
That victory was by no means easy for the young and tired team.
Mars is not a quiet influence by any means this month, astrologers say.
quiet: The result was announced late when the votes were first counted.
She is not the only scientist to question the data from the survey.
His first novel sold slowly, but it earned some good reviews.
We need to finish the bridge using every crew available before winter.
The problem is old; farmers have faced it for centuries.
Le gouvernement a annoncé hier une nouvelle réforme fiscale.
That victory was hard work for the young and tired team.
Mars has a strong influence on passion this month, astrologers say.

notes: Top: 'by no means' (' no' x8), 'by any means', 'par a-illeurs', 'by full rights'. The - pole is the instrumental 'by' (taken by mouth).
